So retrosynthetic break gives carboxylic acid aromatic (the aryl part attached to double bond) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). The carboxylic acid precursor is the α,β‑unsaturated acid after Doebner step? Actually the amide carbonyl is attached to the α,β‑unsaturated chain: /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph. The carboxylic acid precursor would be the α,β‑unsaturated acid: /C=C/C(=O)OH attached to phenyl. So SMILES for that acid: maybe "c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2". plus the aniline "Nc3ccccc3". Good.

Step 2 sulfonamide formation: target has NS(=O)(=O) attached to first phenyl ring (with methyl). So break gives sulfonyl chloride attached to that phenyl: "Cc1ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc1". And the amine part is the other phenyl with sulfonamide nitrogen attached: "Nc2ccc(... )cc2"? Actually the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the second phenyl ring (the one bearing the unsaturated amide). In our disconnection, we treat the sulfonamide nitrogen as part of the amine that later becomes part of the amide step. So the amine precursor is the phenyl bearing the unsaturated acid (the same as step 1 precursor). That amine is "Nc2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2". But we already used that as amine in step 1? Wait step 1 uses aniline (c3ccccc3N) as amine, not the sulfonamide nitrogen. Actually the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the first phenyl (methyl phenyl). The other phenyl (with unsaturated chain) is attached via sulfonamide nitrogen? Let's examine target: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Interpretation: methyl phenyl (c1) has substituent NS(=O)(=O)c2... So the nitrogen attached to methyl phenyl is the sulfonamide nitrogen. That nitrogen is attached to sulfonyl group which is attached to second phenyl (c2). That second phenyl has the unsaturated amide side chain. So sulfonamide nitrogen is part of the chain linking the two phenyls. So retrosynthetic disconnection of sulfonamide gives sulfonyl chloride attached to second phenyl, and the amine is the methyl phenyl with NH (i.e., p-toluidine). So amine precursor: "Cc1ccc(N)cc1". Good.

Thus step 2 precursors: sulfonyl chloride "ClS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2" (attached to second phenyl) and p-toluidine "Cc1ccc(N)cc1". That seems plausible.

Step 3 Doebner modification: break the α,β‑unsaturated acid to aldehyde and malonic acid. The unsaturated acid precursor is "c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2". The aldehyde precursor is "c2ccc(C=O)cc2". Malonic acid is "C(C(=O)O)C(=O)O". Good.
